changes.before: A dataset has eight examples and each batch uses four. After the two batches, what has finished?
changes.after: A batch is one group of examples. An epoch is one pass through them all.

before: A batch is a group of training examples processed for one training update in this simplified loop.
An epoch is one pass through the training dataset. Several batches can fit within one epoch.
Imagine six examples processed two at a time: the first pair, the second pair, and the third pair complete one pass.
Another epoch uses the examples again. Repetition can help learning, but training longer can also worsen overfitting.
Check validation behavior, not only how many passes finished. Batch size and number of epochs are choices about training, not labels assigned to examples.
after: A batch is a group of training examples processed together. In a simple training loop, each batch is used for one parameter update.
An epoch is one full pass through the training examples. It can contain several batches.
A second epoch goes through the training examples again. More passes can help, but too many can increase overfitting.
Watch results on separate validation examples. Finishing more epochs does not by itself show that the model is getting better.

before.question: A dataset has eight examples and each batch uses four. After the two batches, what has finished?
choices: Two epochs, because batch and epoch mean the same thing.
Eight epochs, one for each example.
One epoch: every example has been processed once.
before.explanation: A batch is one group; an epoch is the complete pass through all examples.

after.question: There are 8 examples, split into two batches of 4. Each example is processed once. What finished?
choices: Two epochs, because batch and epoch mean the same thing.
Eight epochs, one for each example.
One epoch: one pass through all eight examples.
after.explanation: Each batch holds four examples. Both batches together finish one full pass.
